transcript.text: Mia: We said we'd plan the outline of that report we've got to write about bicycle theft, remember?
Josh: Hi Mia, yes, let's do it now. Dr Marshall said we should start with a section on the benefits of cycling
as a general background before we discuss the issue of theft.
Mia: Okay, shall we identify the benefits of cycling for society?
Josh: Yes, let's.
Mia: I wondered whether cycling reduces congestion on the roads, but I'm not convinced about it.
What do you think?
Josh: Oh, it must do. I'm sure we can find some data to support that.
Mia: Okay, and I wondered about tourism.
By the sound of it, more visitors are hiring bikes these days.
Josh: Maybe, but a lot more of them like to hire a car instead.
So I don't think that's a valid point, really.
Mia: Okay, should we say something about the safety benefits for pedestrians?
Josh: You mean as versus cars, but cyclists can be a nuisance to pedestrians,
especially if they cycle on the pavements.
Mia: Okay, let's forget that.
Josh: But I don't think there's any doubt that bike use helps us to keep the air clean.
Mia: Agreed.
Josh: Fine. Well, we've got a plan.
Mia: The next sections got to be about the problem, bicycle theft, that is.
Josh: I suggest that we make it very objective.
I mean, by referring to research, I've already got a few facts and figures.
For instance, in the UK, over 376,000 bicycles a year are stolen.
Mia: Wow. It'd be interesting to know how many people whose bikes are stolen actually buy a new one.
Josh: I'll check to see whether there's been any research into that.
Mia: Okay. The government set targets for cycle use.
And I've read that these won't be met now.
It seems that just the threat of having a bike stolen discourages a lot of people from
travelling by bike. It's the second biggest deterrent after fears about road safety.骑自行车出行。这是仅次于道路安全担忧的第二大阻碍因素。
Josh: Yes, I suppose bikes aren't that cheap.
And as far as I know, insurance cover is so expensive, it isn't worth having.
Mia: How much does insurance cost? I mean, for an average bike.
Josh: Hmm, I'm not sure.
Mia: Okay, let me look into that. It'll be good to include some figures.
Josh: Right. I know that in the UK, 17% of cyclists have their bike stolen,
which is why insurance costs are high. It's a lot more common than car theft.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30,
on page 7.
Now listen and answer a questions 25 to 30.
Mia: Okay. Well, now we've got to look at those different bicycle locks and think about their design
features. Have you got a copy of the details?
Josh: Uh, yes. Here. Shall we decide on a particular feature that we like in each case?
What about this handlebar lock?
Mia: Oh, I've never seen one like that. Have you?
It looks complicated.
Josh: Yes, it does. But the brilliant thing is, you have to break the handlebars to remove it.
Mia: Hmm, clever idea. So then the thief hasn't gained anything.
Josh: Right. Then there's this seat lock.
Mia: I think the fact that it isn't heavy is a bonus, don't you?
Josh: Oh, yes. My bike lock weighs a ton.
Mia: Okay. Well, what about the smart lock? It's not particularly sturdy,
but if anyone breaks it, it sprays permanent black ink onto them.
Josh: Yes, and on the bike as well. It helps the police to track it.
Mia: I like that idea. Josh: Me too.
Okay. What do you think of the snake lock?
Mia: I don't think it's particularly strong, but it looks good.
Josh: Yes, it's the only one that's brightly coloured.
I'd like to get one myself.
Mia: And then the pit lock.
Let's see. That's a bit different to the others because it's got lots of components.
It must weigh quite a lot.
Josh: But you attach it to both wheels and the frame and the seat and the handlebars.
It stops thieves from taking any of those bits separately.
Mia: That's a good idea. You often see bikes that have had a wheel stolen or something.
Josh: Then there's the axle lock. Apparently, it's so straightforward that you can lock
any bike with it in under 10 seconds. Mia: I could do with one of those.
That is the end of section 3. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
Now turn to section 4.
